hook.text: J.I. Rodale brought organic farming to America in 1942. Doctors and scientists called him a crank.

buildup.text: Rodale published Organic Farming and Gardening magazine, preaching composting and chemical-free growing.

discovery.text: His Farming Systems Trial—started in 1981—is the longest-running comparison of organic and conventional farming.

twist.text: After 40 years, the trial shows organic yields match conventional after a transition period—with lower input costs.

climax.text: Rodale's once-fringe ideas are now mainstream. Organic food is a $200 billion global industry.

punchline.text: The crank was right. It just took 80 years for the world to listen.

quiz.question: What does the Rodale Farming Systems Trial show after 40 years?
options: Organic yields match conventional after transition, with lower input costs
